citations.title: What Sales and market does and does not claim
citations.location: Operator guidance: what-this-feature-does; section Where the sale records come from; chars 421-1251
citations.excerpt:
## Where the sale records come from

Sale observations arrive as a checksum-protected release published by the Property data research
area, which sources them from NSW property sales information. Sales and market does not collect
records from publishers directly and does not fetch anything from the internet when you open a
case.

Each sale carries its contract date, recorded price, match tier, match confidence, the source
release it arrived in, and whether the record is synthetic demonstration data. Every summary names
the source releases it drew on, so a number on screen can be traced back to the release that
supplied it.

Current record counts, release identifiers and case contents are live database facts. Ask the
assistant for those; they are answered from the feature's read-only tools rather than from this
guidance.

citations.title: What Sales and market does and does not claim
citations.location: Operator guidance: what-this-feature-does; section How to build a market case; chars 1254-2136
citations.excerpt:
## How to build a market case

Choose New case, give it a descriptive name, and select the property by its address. Confirm the
address is the one you meant, then set the start and end dates for the period you want to study.

Set the status to Draft, Active, Complete or Archived, and choose the minimum match tier. Tier A
is the strictest; the default minimum is tier B. Add research notes if they help you remember why
the case exists, then choose Save case.

Selecting a saved case from the Market cases list shows its eligible sale count, median recorded
price, excluded-record count, source-release count, and volume by contract year. Use Edit to
change the name, date window, status, match threshold or notes. Edits use optimistic version
checking, so if the case changed elsewhere since you opened it, your update is rejected rather
than silently overwriting the other change.

citations.title: What Sales and market evidence cannot establish
citations.location: Operator guidance: evidence-limits; section Demonstration data; chars 1908-2415
citations.excerpt:
## Demonstration data

Some cases include deterministic synthetic showcase data so the workflow can be demonstrated
without real records. Where that is so, the summary says the case includes synthetic showcase
data. Those figures exist to show the mechanics and must never be quoted as evidence about a real
property or a real market.

A case whose records are synthetic cannot support any claim about actual sales activity, and no
conclusion about a real suburb, street or property should be drawn from one.

citations.title: What Sales and market evidence cannot establish
citations.location: Operator guidance: evidence-limits; section Coverage gaps and excluded records; chars 1169-1905
citations.excerpt:
## Coverage gaps and excluded records

A summary reports only the sales that passed the case filters, and separately counts what it left
out. Records are excluded for four reasons: no contract date, a contract date outside the case
period, a missing or zero price, or a match tier below the threshold you selected.

Excluded records are not errors and are not deleted. Raising the minimum match tier deliberately
narrows the evidence, so a case with few eligible sales may reflect a strict threshold rather than
a quiet market.

Where fewer than three sales are eligible, the summary states that this is insufficient evidence.
Treat the median from such a case as an observation about those specific records, not a
representative figure.

citations.title: How sales are attributed to a property and how confident that is
citations.location: Operator guidance: match-quality; section Reading a summary honestly; chars 1036-1637
citations.excerpt:
## Reading a summary honestly

The eligible sale count and the excluded count should be read together. A median drawn from three
eligible sales with twelve excluded is a much weaker statement than the same median drawn from
thirty, and the summary reports both so the difference stays visible.

Volume by contract year shows when the eligible sales occurred. Gaps in that series mean no
eligible sale was registered in those years for this property at this threshold. They do not mean
the property was unavailable, unsold or unoccupied, and they are not evidence of market conditions
in the wider area.
